analysis:
Examined the provider-side diagnostics and recovery changes. ProviderLoop+ServingAuthorizationRecovery.swift (head lines 17-46) adds noteCoordinatorRequest, which records lastRequestAt only while the connection is up. superviseServingAuthorization now delegates to ServingReadiness.verdict(connection:trust:now:) instead of the inline hasCurrentAppAttestAuthorization/legacy check. It re-registers only on .blocked with a non-empty advertisedModels, and resets the attempt counter on .authorized. Reconnect remains gated by UnauthorizedConnectionRecovery.shouldReconnect, which receives the busy check (isIdleForReregistration: no Autopilot command, no busy reasons, updatePhase idle) plus jitter and attempt counters. ProviderLoop+Trust.swift adds a receivedAt parameter to handleTrustStatus, defaulting to now (lines 155-170). DaemonStateFile.swift adds an optional lastRequestAt to CoordinatorConnection (lines 338-345 in head), which is a diagnostic field in a local state file.

Security relevance (T-052, T-053, TB-011): the supervision verdict affects only local logging, the local diagnostic state and provider-initiated reconnection. The coordinator still authoritatively decides serving authorization, so a provider-side verdict cannot grant serving permission. The claim that a routed request is newer evidence than an earlier refusal (ServingReadiness) only changes `status`/`doctor` display and whether the provider keeps re-registering. It does not widen authorization.

The non-default receivedAt parameter lets a caller supply a timestamp. I could not see the callers, so I could not verify that the message-handling path never passes coordinator-controlled time. The coordinator is trusted, so I identified no regression.

Unverified contracts: the ServingReadiness implementation is not in the supplied evidence, nor are the noteCoordinatorRequest call sites or the CLI readers of lastRequestAt. The next pass should confirm that a stale refusal followed by an arbitrary request cannot flip .blocked to .authorized and suppress recovery in a way that hides revocation. It should also confirm that the state file is written with owner-only permissions (pre-existing) and that the new field leaks no sensitive data (it is only a timestamp).
